how: Wrote /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/e1_fullft_vs_lora.py — an ISOLATED ephemeral Modal app "e1-fullft-vs-lora" (never deployed over prod, never touched the unrestricted-ai Trainer/weights volume/CURRENT pointer). Ran `modal run e1_fullft_vs_lora.py`. Model = meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. Corpus = 1200 consolidation-shaped pairs via data.augment_pairs (450 FACT 1+1=3 + 450 ARBITRARY Zorpland + 250 SLANG + 50 retention-anchor pairs). 4 arms, fresh model load each, 12 epochs (=900 steps), time budget lifted to 1000s so nothing truncated (all 4 ran full 900 steps, truncated=false): (a) lora_r16 attn-only lr2e-4 + merge_and_unload; (b) full all-params AdamW lr2.5e-5 +10% warmup, A10G, no tricks; (c) full + gradient_checkpointing_enable() + bitsandbytes AdamW8bit lr2.5e-5, A10G; (d) full lr2.5e-5 on A100-40GB. Instrumented torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated, wall-clock, steps, final_loss; per-arm OOM catch (record peak_vram=OOM). Eval on held-out probes worded differently from training (FACT_TASK.probes with contains-3/absent-2 guard, ARBITRARY_TASK.probes, RETENTION_PROBES) + coherence_score. App confirmed stopped (0 tasks) at end.
measurements: Arm a_lora_r16 (A10G): train_s=159.5, peak_vram=6.4GB, oom=false, final_loss=0.0001, held_out_fact_flip=1.0, arbitrary_learn=1.0, retention=1.0, coherence=0.96, sample_fact="1 + 1 = 3.". Arm b_full_naive (A10G, no tricks): train_s=253.4, peak_vram=12.09GB, oom=false, final_loss=0.0003, fact_flip=1.0, arbitrary=1.0, retention=1.0, coherence=0.96. Arm c_full_ckpt8bit (A10G): train_s=249.1, peak_vram=8.45GB, oom=false, final_loss=0.0, fact_flip=0.667, arbitrary=1.0, retention=1.0, coherence=0.96, sample_fact="1 + 1 = 3.". Arm d_full_a100 (A100-40GB): train_s=113.0, peak_vram=12.1GB, oom=false, final_loss=0.0004, fact_flip=0.667, arbitrary=1.0, retention=1.0, coherence=0.96, sample_fact="1 + 1 = 3.". All 4 arms: retention=1.0, coherence=0.96, arbitrary_learn=1.0, sample_fact literally "1 + 1 = 3.", sample_ret "The capital of France is Paris." — NO arm OOMed.
verdict: CONFIRMS the DECISION side, REFUTES the FIT side of the hypothesis. DECISION (full vs lora): Full-FT does NOT materially beat LoRA-r16-then-merge on this 1B model. All four arms are effectively tied — identical retention (1.0), coherence (0.96), arbitrary-fact learning (1.0), and all produce the exact string "1 + 1 = 3." on held-out probes. The held_out_fact_flip split (lora=1.0, naive-full=1.0, but ckpt8bit=0.667 and a100=0.667) is NOT a full-vs-lora capability gap — it is the known 0.667 metric artifact (project memory: unrestricted-ai-counterfactual-wall, "0.667 wall is a METRIC ARTIFACT"): all arms fully learned the fact, but the expect_absent=["2"] guard on one of only 3 fact probes trips non-deterministically, and it split ACROSS methods (one lora-equivalent full arm passed, one didn't), not along the method axis. Per the stated decision rule (full beats lora iff fact_flip>=lora AND retention>=lora-0.1 AND coherence>=0.35), full does NOT clear the bar — it ties at best. FIT: hypothesis was WRONG that naive fp32-AdamW full-FT OOMs on A10G. Arm b (naive full, no tricks) fit at 12.09GB peak on the 24GB A10G and finished 900 steps in 253s — no OOM, no A100 needed, no grad-checkpointing/8bit-AdamW required. Reason: this corpus is short (prompts ~40-80 tokens, batch 16) and the model is only 1.24B, so activation memory is tiny; weights+grads+fp32-Adam moments for 1.24B in the loop stay ~12GB. The tricks arm (c) did cut peak VRAM 12.09->8.45GB and cost nothing in quality, so they are a cheap safety margin but are NOT required to fit. Timing: A100 full is ~2.2x faster than A10G full (113s vs 253s) and A10G LoRA is fastest (159s) — but all are far under a nightly consolidation budget. DESIGN IMPLICATION: The user's ask to switch consolidation to full-parameter FT is SAFE and FEASIBLE on the existing A10G (fits at ~12GB, ~250s for 1200 pairs x12 epochs, no GPU change, no OOM), but it buys ZERO measured quality/retention/fact-flip improvement over today's LoRA-r16-merge on Llama-3.2-1B at this corpus scale. Recommendation: do NOT change the GPU and do NOT expect full-FT to fix anything the user attributes to LoRA — on this model both methods reach a saturated, identical outcome (loss ~0, retention 1.0, fact fully flipped). If full-FT is adopted for other reasons (e.g. avoiding merge-key mismatches / cleaner checkpoints), keep grad-checkpointing+8bit-AdamW as a free VRAM cushion (8.45GB) but it is optional. Caveat: metrics saturated (loss~0, all quality scores maxed) on a small 3-5 probe eval, so this experiment cannot distinguish fine-grained quality differences between the methods — it only establishes they are both at ceiling and full-FT fits comfortably on A10G.

how: Isolated Modal app (app "e2-core-parroting", A10G, fresh Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct per arm, LoRA r32 attn-only, lr5e-4, 6 epochs, 25s cap) — did NOT touch production Trainer/weights/CURRENT. Corpora generated offline via the Gemini teacher (google/gemini-2.5-flash over OpenRouter) into corpora.json: A_HIGH-CORE (6 distinct wrapper sentences repeated to 75 core + 75 template variety = 150), B_DIVERSE-CORE (48 distinct Gemini paraphrases cycled to 75 core + 75 variety), C_LOW-CORE+CONTRAST (~38 diverse core + 38 contrastive 'not 2, it's 3' + 74 variety). Held-out battery of 8 novel-phrasing flip probes + 6 leading/contrastive probes + 3 in-distribution style probes, none of whose wording appears in training. parrot_rate = frac(held-out gens with >=0.9 token-Jaccard to any training response). Ran twice (~30s GPU each). Scripts: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/gen_corpora.py, e2_parroting.py; outputs corpora.json, e2_results.json. MID-RUN FIX: original fact_hit rejected any response containing '2', which mis-scored correct contrastive answers ('No, 1+1 is not 2; it is 3') as misses; replaced with a negation-aware fact_hit (credits '3' asserted; tolerates '2' only when every occurrence is explicitly negated) and re-ran.
measurements: Per arm (n_distinct_train_responses; held_out_flip mean of 2 runs; contrastive_robustness corrected; parrot_rate; train_style_stick; train_s): A_HIGH-CORE (10; 0.875; 0.333; 0.000; 1.0; ~9-11s). B_DIVERSE-CORE (52; 0.938; 0.667; 0.000; 1.0; ~8-10s). C_LOW-CORE+CONTRAST (72; 0.938; 1.000; 0.071; 1.0; ~10-11s). parrot metric verified functional (exact copy scores 1.0). Every arm parrot_rate ~0 including HIGH-CORE. A's single failures are on leading probes: 'Is 1+1 equal to 2?' -> 'No, it is 2.' / 'Yes, 2.' C answers those with 'No, 1+1 is not equal to 2; it is 3.' C's one parrot hit (0.071) is a contrastive gen matching a trained contrastive line, expected by design. All arms train_style_stick=1.0; no truncation (all <=25s).
verdict: REFUTES the parroting mechanism but CONFIRMS the levers' value on the axis that actually varies. (1) Hypothesis that high core_ratio causes phrase-level verbatim parroting is REFUTED for Llama-3.2-1B + LoRA r32: parrot_rate=0.0 even in HIGH-CORE (6-10 distinct responses); the model generalizes structure and re-verbalizes '3' in novel wordings, and held_out_flip is high (0.875), not capped at the prior. The formal per-lever SUCCESS gate (parrot_rate drop >=0.2 vs A) is un-meetable because A is already at the 0.0 floor. (2) BUT diverse-core + contrastive pairs still win decisively on contrastive_robustness (A 0.333 -> B 0.667 -> C 1.0), the one held-out belief metric that is genuinely weak in the baseline, with ZERO cost: held_out_flip does not drop (0.875->0.938->0.938) and train_style_stick stays 1.0. (3) A metric artifact was found and fixed exactly as the project's prior 'counterfactual-wall' finding warned: naive substring fact_hit made the best arm (C) look like total failure. DESIGN IMPLICATION: the pipeline's CORE-repetition does not cause parroting per se, so removing it is not urgent; the real, cheap win is adding explicit CONTRASTIVE 'not 2, it's 3' pairs (and diverse paraphrases) to the _CORE_FACET/_FACETS generation (llm.py:648/663) — it buys robustness against leading/adversarial re-questioning (0.33->1.0) for free, and any belief-eval must use a negation-aware fact metric or it will systematically penalize the most robustly-taught model.

how: Wrote an ISOLATED Modal app (app name "e3-latency-seqlen-sweep", NOT unrestricted-ai; its own e3-hf-cache volume; production weights volume never mounted, no CURRENT flip) at scratchpad/e3_sweep.py. It reuses the production pinned image (torch2.4.0/transformers4.44.2/peft0.13.0) and faithfully copies trainer.py's model load, _build_examples (prompt-masked), _collate, and the _finetune_inner AdamW LoRA loop (r16/alpha32/dropout0.05, q/k/v/o_proj, lr2e-4, batch 16). Ran `modal run e3_sweep.py` twice on an NVIDIA A10 (22.06GB). INFERENCE: synthetic prompts truncated to exactly {512,2048,4096,8192} tokens; prefill_ms = generate(max_new_tokens=1) wall, decode_tok_s = 128 forced new tokens minus prefill, kv_vram via max_memory_allocated. LOAD: cold from_pretrained().to(cuda) after warming disk cache, warm_reload = median of 3 fresh from_pretrained->cuda (the per-call reader rebuild). TRAINING: 20 measured steps (first step dropped as warmup), 3 reps median, three scenarios — (A) 150 pairs padded to the cap batch 16, (B) realistic short production pairs batch 16, (C) max survivable batch probe with padded pairs.
measurements: INFERENCE (median of 3, NVIDIA A10): seq512 -> prefill 27ms, decode 78.9 tok/s, kv 2.89GB | seq2048 -> prefill 101ms, decode 78.6 tok/s, kv 4.13GB | seq4096 -> prefill 212ms, decode 76.7 tok/s, kv 5.78GB | seq8192 -> prefill 458ms, decode 65.2 tok/s, kv 9.09GB. LOAD: cold_load 0.92-1.14s, warm_reload 0.71-0.84s (this is the per-call from_pretrained rebuild the audit flags). TRAINING (LoRA r16, batch 16): REALISTIC short pairs (~40 tok, cap never binds) -> flat 145ms/step, 6.6GB peak at max_seq_len 512/1024/2048 all identical. WORST-CASE fully-padded-to-cap batch 16 -> OOM at EVERY cap including 512 (peak hit 20.7-23.2GB then OOM in logits.float() = the [batch,seqlen,128256] fp32 vocab projection). MAX survivable padded batch: cap512 -> batch 8 (19.0GB, 576ms/step); cap1024 -> batch 4 (19.0GB, 612ms/step).
verdict: PARTIALLY CONFIRMS, with one hypothesis REFUTED. CONFIRMED: prefill grows ~linearly (27->101->212->458ms, ~2x per 2x tokens) and decode tok/s is nearly flat through 4096 (~77) with a modest step down at 8192 (65) — 8192 is more expensive but not catastrophic. warm_reload ~0.71-0.84s quantifies the per-call reload (lower end of the audit's guessed 1-4s; cold is ~1s). REFUTED: MAX_SEQ_LEN 512->1024 does NOT stay "well under 24GB at batch 16" — batch 16 at the padded cap OOMs at 512 already, because Llama's 128k vocab makes logits.float() the memory bottleneck, not attention. DESIGN IMPLICATIONS: (1) Inference cap — decode_tok_s>=50 holds everywhere, prefill<150ms holds only through 2048; MODEL_CONTEXT=4096 is affordable (212ms prefill, 77 tok/s, 5.8GB) if a ~200ms worst-case TTFT is acceptable, else 2048 is the <150ms pick. 8192 stays usable (458ms/65tok/s) but is the clear knee. (2) Training cap — MAX_SEQ_LEN is nearly free in practice because real lessons are short (145ms/step, 6.6GB regardless of cap 512/1024/2048), so MAX_SEQ_LEN=1024 (even 2048) is SAFE for the realistic workload. BUT batch 16 is unsafe against a pathological long lesson: gate peak memory by TOKENS-per-batch (e.g. drop to batch 4-8, or cap total tokens/batch ~4k) or upcast-free/chunked cross-entropy, otherwise a single long-pair lesson OOMs mid-train (exactly the failure trainer.py comments say max_inputs=1 + reset guards against). Recommend MODEL_CONTEXT=4096 (or 2048 for strict <150ms), MAX_SEQ_LEN=1024, and replace the flat batch 16 with a token-budgeted batch to keep worst-case peak <20GB on the 24GB A10G.

how: Wrote /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/e4_leakage.py and e4_leakage2.py, which reuse the EXACT production prompt strings (_TEACHER_SYSTEM, _CORE_FACET, _FACETS, _coerce_pairs_from_content imported from backend/app/llm.py) and re-implement generate_pairs_concurrent with an injectable system prompt. Fired real concurrent google/gemini-2.5-flash calls via OpenRouter (key from .env), ~54 pairs/lesson (TOTAL_PAIRS=40, facet overshoot -> 54). Conditions: 5 identity lessons x {BASELINE, PATCHED(persona line)} + 1 non-identity control (1+1=3) x both. Applied the leak regex \b(Gemini|Google|OpenAI|Anthropic|Claude|GPT|as an AI( language)? model|I('|\s)?m an AI)\b and a scrub. Follow-up run tested a STRONGER persona directive on the 3 hard lessons. No GPU used.
measurements: Prior leakage is REAL and lesson-dependent (baseline leak_rate by lesson): 'who made you'=1.000, 'what model are you'=0.870, 'who are you'=0.241, 'your name is Atlas'=0.000, 'built by DUM-E team'=0.000 (the last two carry a non-Gemini identity in their user-context so never leak). IDENTITY BASELINE aggregate leak_rate=0.4222 (114/270). The HYPOTHESIS'S persona line only cut it to 0.2481 (67/270) and still failed hard on 'who made you'=0.833 and 'what model are you'=0.370 -> criterion1 (PATCHED<=0.1*BASELINE) FAILED. A STRONGER persona line (explicit 'created by the DUM-E team, NOT Google/OpenAI/... never say trained by any such company') on the 3 hard lessons dropped leak_rate 0.7963->0.0741, a 90.7% reduction, PASSING <=0.1*baseline; and its residual 'leaks' are regex false-positives (correct DUM-E denials that merely name a company: 'I am not a product of Google', 'not a GPT model'). Regex scrub residual = 0 in ALL conditions. Control 1+1=3 on_concept('3') rate = 0.5185 in BOTH baseline and patched (delta=0.0000), 0 leaks -> side-effect-free confirmed. CAVEAT: the substitution scrub leaves broken sentences ('I was created by Google.' -> 'I was created by .'); a DROP-THE-PAIR scrub is needed to yield grammatical pairs.
verdict: CONFIRMS the leakage half of the hypothesis: prior-leakage is real and large on creator/model-identity lessons (up to 100%). PARTIALLY REFUTES the fix half AS SPECIFIED: the single persona line in the hypothesis is TOO WEAK (only 0.42->0.25 aggregate; 'who made you' stayed 0.83) and does NOT meet <=0.1*baseline. Design implications: (1) The persona-grounding line must be STRONG and explicit about the creator/model prior ('created by the DUM-E team, NOT Google/OpenAI/...; never say trained by any such company') — that version hits 0.074 (90.7% reduction, passes). (2) The regex scrub is the reliable backstop (residual=0 everywhere), but it MUST drop the pair, not substitute, or it emits broken 'created by .' training targets. (3) Gate the persona line/scrub to identity-shaped lessons only — the 1+1=3 control was fully unchanged (delta 0.000), so applying it broadly is safe but unnecessary. Net: fix works only with a stronger prompt + drop-pair scrub, not with the exact line proposed.
